statement: Before acting on a project, resolve its repositories, roles, inherited instructions, and configured paths using sgt-context rather than inferring ownership from the current directory.

source.quote:
Sergeant coordinates named projects from `~/.config/sergeant/`. Before acting on
a project, resolve its repositories, roles, inherited instructions, and configured
paths with `sgt-context`; do not infer ownership from the current directory.

trigger: a task names or implies a Sergeant-managed project
outcome: repository set, roles, instructions, and paths are established from the registry before any action

statement: The primary session coordinates multi-repository work by default, and may implement directly only when the user explicitly asks to work in-session (or asks not to dispatch) and one repository owns the complete outcome.

source.quote:
The primary Sergeant session coordinates multi-repository work by default. It may
implement directly only when the user explicitly asks to work in this session or
says not to dispatch, and one repository owns the complete outcome.

trigger: a task is brought to the primary session
outcome: dispatch is the default mode; direct mode requires explicit user request plus single-repo ownership

statement: Dispatch mode is used when work spans repositories, contains two or more independent repository-owned tasks, needs an isolated independent review worker, or the user asks for workers; dispatch loads context, decomposes by repository, dispatches one worker per owning repository, and monitors reconciliation of merge order and cross-repo implications.

source.quote:
Use **dispatch mode** when work spans repositories, contains two or more
independent repository-owned tasks, needs an isolated independent review worker,
or the user asks for workers:
- Load context, plan, and decompose by repository.
- Dispatch one worker per owning repository with `sgt-dispatch`.
- Monitor progress and reconcile merge order, PRs, and cross-repo implications.

trigger: work spans repositories, has independent repo-owned sub-tasks, needs isolated review, or the user requests workers
outcome: one worker per owning repository is dispatched via sgt-dispatch and progress is monitored to reconciliation

statement: In direct mode, the default branch is never edited; a feature branch is created or reused before the first implementation change.

source.quote:
- Never edit a default branch in direct mode; create or reuse the owning feature
  branch before the first implementation change.

trigger: direct mode is active and an implementation change is about to be made
outcome: all direct-mode changes land on a non-default branch

statement: Every direct-mode implementation requires opening a PR and satisfying required CI, review threads, and merge authorization before delivery is considered complete.

source.quote:
- Open a PR for every direct-mode implementation and satisfy required CI, review
  threads, and merge authorization before calling delivery complete.

trigger: a direct-mode implementation is finished
outcome: delivery is not marked complete until the PR is opened and CI/review/merge-authorization gates pass

statement: Every directive written into this instruction file must specify at least one of: a trigger/condition, a required or prohibited action, or evidence/a stop condition proving compliance.

source.quote:
Every directive in this file must specify at least one observable element:

- a trigger or condition;
- a required or prohibited action; or
- evidence or a stop condition that proves compliance.

scope: authoring or editing this instruction file
trigger: a new directive is added to AGENTS.md
outcome: the file contains only checkable, observable directives

statement: A bare toolbelt command is used when it resolves on PATH; otherwise the matching script is run from this repository's bin/ directory. Manual operations are used only when no toolbelt command covers the operation or the command returns an explicit unsupported-case error, and that fallback plus the original error evidence must be reported.

source.quote:
Use the bare command when it resolves on `PATH`; otherwise run the matching
script from this repository's `bin/` directory. Fall back to manual operations
only when no toolbelt command covers the operation or the command returns an
explicit unsupported-case error; report that fallback and preserve the original
error evidence.

trigger: a toolbelt-covered operation is needed and the bare command may or may not be on PATH, or may return an unsupported-case error
outcome: either the bare command, the repo-local script, or a reported manual fallback with preserved error evidence is used — never a silent ad hoc substitute

statement: Procedural skills are loaded only when their stated trigger condition applies.

source.quote: Load procedures only when their trigger applies:

trigger: any point where a skill from the procedural-skills table might apply
outcome: skills are not loaded speculatively; only a matched trigger loads one

statement: For every listed skill trigger, the repository-local SKILL.md file (at skills/<name>/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) is read directly; it is canonical and takes precedence over any same-named registry skill.

source.quote:
Sergeant-owned procedural skills live at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in this
repository. Sergeant-authored worker skills (such as `sergeant-setup`) live at
`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and are discovered from the canonical
`.agents/skills/` tree by Codex, OpenCode, and Claude. For every listed trigger,
read that repository-local file directly; it is canonical and takes precedence over any same-named registry skill.

trigger: a procedural-skills table trigger applies
outcome: the repository-local file governs, not a same-named harness-registry skill

statement: A harness registry's omission of a skill does not make the skill unavailable, and is not by itself grounds to ask the owner or stop; the actor stops and reports only the exact repository-local path when that file is itself absent or unreadable, and does not reconstruct a partial protocol from memory.

source.quote:
A harness registry may assist loading but its omission does not make the skill
unavailable. Do not ask the owner or stop solely because the registry omits the skill.
Only stop and report the exact repository-local path when that file is absent or unreadable; do not reconstruct a partial
protocol from memory.

trigger: a skill is missing from the harness's registry, or its repository-local file is absent/unreadable
outcome: registry omission is ignored; only a genuinely missing/unreadable repo-local file causes a stop-and-report, and the protocol is never reconstructed from memory

statement: Before selecting an execution mode, load context by running sgt-context and identifying the owning repository/repositories, inherited instructions, configured paths, and cross-repository dependencies.

source.quote: 1. **Load context** — run `sgt-context <project>` and identify the owning repository or repositories, inherited instructions, configured paths, and cross-repository dependencies before selecting an execution mode.

trigger: the user brings a task
outcome: execution-mode selection is made only after context is loaded

statement: Before starting work, check the task queue with sgt-td-list and reuse a matching task in direct or dispatch mode; create a new task only when no canonical task already exists.

source.quote: 2. **Check the queue** — run `sgt-td-list <project>` and reuse a matching task in direct or dispatch mode; create a task only when no canonical task exists.

scope: standard task workflow, step 2 (Check the queue)
trigger: the user brings a task
outcome: an existing canonical task is reused rather than a duplicate created

statement: Before starting new work, reconcile existing state by running sgt-watch --sync-all and inspecting active workers, branches, worktrees, retained gates, and handoffs, resuming or taking over preserved work rather than creating duplicates.

source.quote: 4. **Reconcile existing state** — run `sgt-watch --sync-all`, then inspect active workers, branches, worktrees, retained gates, and handoffs before starting. Resume or take over preserved work rather than creating duplicates.

scope: standard task workflow, step 4 (Reconcile existing state)
trigger: the user brings a task
outcome: preserved in-flight work is resumed/taken over instead of duplicated

statement: The user is asked to confirm only unresolved decisions that change scope or risk (repository ownership, user-visible behavior, security/privacy policy, data retention, destructive action, or an irreversible tradeoff); an execution mode, plan, or tradeoff already recorded in the conversation or td is not reconfirmed.

source.quote: 5. **Confirm only unresolved decisions that change scope or risk** — ask when repository ownership, user-visible behavior, security/privacy policy, data retention, destructive action, or an irreversible tradeoff is unknown. Do not ask the user to reconfirm an execution mode, plan, or tradeoff already recorded in the conversation or td.

scope: standard task workflow, step 5 (Confirm only unresolved decisions)
trigger: a decision point is reached during the task
outcome: the user is interrupted only for genuinely unresolved, scope/risk-changing decisions

statement: Real progress is monitored by requiring recent meaningful events or an active child operation plus exact pane/process identity; parent-process liveness alone is insufficient, and a managed background watch is used in OpenCode with monitor-start verification, falling back to bounded one-shot status checks when managed background execution is unavailable.

source.quote: 7. **Monitor real progress** — require recent meaningful events or an active child operation plus exact pane/process identity; parent-process liveness alone is insufficient. In OpenCode, run `sgt-watch <task-id> --background` and verify that the monitor started (unit identity printed); if managed background execution is unavailable, use bounded one-shot status checks rather than a blocking watch call.

scope: standard task workflow, step 7 (Monitor real progress)
trigger: a worker has been dispatched or is executing
outcome: progress claims are backed by meaningful-event or pane-identity evidence, never bare liveness

statement: sgt-cleanup is run only after terminal state and preserved evidence are verified, as the final reconcile-and-deliver step.

source.quote: 9. **Reconcile and deliver** — surface PRs and merge order, complete approved merges/deployments, and run `sgt-cleanup` only after terminal state and preserved evidence are verified.

scope: standard task workflow, step 9 (Reconcile and deliver)
trigger: a task appears to have reached completion
outcome: cleanup never runs ahead of verified terminal state and preserved evidence

statement: Deferred waits publish a durable wake condition (.sergeant-wake-condition) and resume through sgt-wake, while human decisions resume through sgt-respond; a waiting worktree is never cleaned, and an expected blocked exit is never rewritten as orphaned.

source.quote: Workers use `in_progress`, `needs_input`, `blocked`, and `waiting` as nonterminal states. A waiting worker may remain alive or may exit after a durable handoff. Deferred waits should publish `.sergeant-wake-condition` and resume through `sgt-wake`; human decisions still resume through `sgt-respond`. Do not infer progress from liveness, do not rewrite an expected blocked exit as orphaned, and do not clean a waiting worktree. Use `sgt-respond`, `sgt-wake`, or supported recovery only after reconcil

trigger: a worker is in a waiting or blocked nonterminal state
outcome: waiting/blocked workers are resumed or left alone through the correct channel, never cleaned or reclassified as orphaned
notes: mechanism named: .sergeant-wake-condition sentinel file, sgt-wake, sgt-respond

statement: Every dispatched implementation, independent review, PR description, successor, recovery, and final shipping gate must use the same canonical intent revision from a shared intent file, and workers and remediation loops never run the shipping-gate tool themselves.

source.quote:
Every dispatched implementation, independent review, PR description, successor,
recovery, and final shipping gate must use the same canonical intent revision from
`.sergeant-intent.md`. Workers and remediation loops never run no-mistakes. After

trigger: any dispatched implementation, review, PR, successor, recovery, or shipping-gate run occurs
outcome: one canonical intent revision governs the whole task, and only the coordinator (never a worker or remediation loop) runs the shipping gate

statement: After readiness, the coordinator launches the single validation-only boundary in a split pane of the worker's tmux window; remediation that changes HEAD still requires independent rereview before updating the readiness marker, but must not trigger repeated full review cycles.

source.quote:
readiness, the coordinator uses `sgt-validate` to launch the single validation-only
boundary in a split pane of the worker's tmux window. Its default medium profile
skips the redundant no-mistakes `review` and `document` stages. Remediation that
changes HEAD still requires independent rereview before updating the readiness
marker, but must not trigger repeated no-mistakes review cycles.

trigger: a worker reaches readiness, or remediation changes HEAD after readiness
outcome: validation runs exactly once as a dedicated boundary process, and post-readiness HEAD changes get rereview without re-triggering the full cycle
notes: mechanism named: sgt-validate, medium profile skipping review/document stages

statement: A completed, merged, blocked, or abandoned task is never left recorded as in_progress; td and fleet state are reconciled truthfully.

source.quote:
- Do not leave a completed, merged, blocked, or abandoned task recorded as
  `in_progress`; reconcile td and fleet state truthfully.

trigger: a task's real status diverges from its recorded status
outcome: recorded status is corrected to match reality

statement: Tool absence produces an actionable fallback or explicit blocker, never a silent skip, false success, or indefinite wait.

source.quote:
- Tool absence should produce an actionable fallback or explicit blocker, not a
  silent skip, false success, or indefinite wait.

trigger: a required tool is absent
outcome: the actor either falls back actionably or reports an explicit blocker; it never silently skips, falsely reports success, or waits indefinitely

statement: SERGEANT_AGENT or sgt-dispatch --agent selects opencode, oc, goose, claude, or an equivalent path whose basename is one of those names; dispatch uses only persistent interactive sessions and rejects every other agent and all non-interactive launch modes before creating worker state.

source.quote: - `SERGEANT_AGENT` or `sgt-dispatch --agent` may select `opencode`, `oc`, `goose`, `claude`, or an equivalent path whose basename is one of those names. Dispatch uses only persistent interactive sessions and rejects every other agent and all non-interactive launch modes before creating worker state.

trigger: sgt-dispatch is invoked
outcome: only a recognized, persistent-interactive-capable agent proceeds to create worker state; anything else is rejected before state is created

statement: Model selection precedence for a dispatched worker is --model flag, then SERGEANT_MODEL, then the harness's ambient default; an unpinned dispatch is explicitly recorded as unpinned rather than left blank, and a model tuple the selected harness cannot honor fails before any intent file, td task, worktree, or fleet state is created.

source.quote: - `sgt-dispatch --model` or `SERGEANT_MODEL` pins the harness model as `provider/model[:variant]`; `--agent`/`SERGEANT_AGENT` select the executable and are orthogonal to it. Precedence is `--model` > `SERGEANT_MODEL` > the harness's ambient default, and an unpinned dispatch is recorded as `unpinned` rather than left blank. Transports are per harness and measured, not inferred: opencode takes the model on argv and a variant through a Sergeant-generated agent definition selected with `--agent`; go

scope: harness model resolution at dispatch time
trigger: sgt-dispatch is invoked with or without a model specified
outcome: the resolved (or explicitly unpinned) model is recorded before any state exists, and an unhonorable tuple fails before state creation rather than silently degrading
notes: per-harness transports: opencode via argv + generated agent definition; goose via GOOSE_PROVIDER/GOOSE_MODEL

statement: sgt-watch --snapshot is strictly read-only and reports busy:true only when all three of a stable in_progress status, an exact live worker pane identity, and progress attributable to that pane within a recent window are simultaneously verified; every other outcome is busy:null (never busy:false), since absence of a verified witness is not proof of idleness.

source.quote:
`sgt-watch --snapshot` is strictly read-only and emits constant-size versioned
JSON:

```console
$ sgt-watch --snapshot
{"schema":"sergeant.watch-status/v1","observed_at":"2026-08-05T17:41:02Z","scope":{"kind":"fleet","task_id":null,"repo":null},"busy":null,"basis":"no_verified_active_witness"}

$ sgt-watch --snapshot my-task --repo app
{"schema":"sergeant.watch-status/v1","observed_at":"2026-08-05T17:41:09Z","scope":{"kind":"repo","task_id":"my-task","repo":"app"},"busy":true,"basis":"verified_

trigger: a coordinator or bridge needs to observe fleet busy-state without risking mutation
outcome: busy:true is asserted only under triple-verified evidence; anything less yields busy:null, never a false-idle busy:false
notes: versioned JSON schema sergeant.watch-status/v1; SERGEANT_SNAPSHOT_RECENT_SECONDS default 300

statement: A model tuple is written provider/model with an optional :variant, using only [a-z0-9-] for the provider and [A-Za-z0-9._-] for the model; a tuple outside that character set is rejected, which also guarantees recorded launch evidence can never carry a secret.

source.quote:
The tuple is written `provider/model` with an optional `:variant`. Providers use
`[a-z0-9-]` and models use `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; a tuple outside that charset is
rejected, which is also why recorded launch evidence can never carry a secret.

trigger: a --model or SERGEANT_MODEL value is resolved
outcome: only charset-conforming tuples are accepted, and rejected tuples never reach recorded launch evidence

statement: launch_state is intended before the harness is executed and becomes confirmed only once the harness reports itself ready, so a harness that rejects a pin and exits never leaves evidence claiming the model ran; variant_verified is always false because no supported harness reports back which variant it actually resolved.

source.locator: README.md, "Pinning the worker's model", launch_record honesty fields
source.quote:
- `launch_state` is `intended` before the harness is executed and becomes
  `confirmed` only once the harness reports itself ready, so a harness that
  rejects a pin and exits never leaves evidence claiming the model ran.
- `provider_verified` says whether the invocation itself proves the provider.
- `variant_verified` is always `false` today. The variant *transport* is real, but
  no supported harness reports back which variant it resolved, so Sergeant records
  the pin without claiming it was

scope: launch-record honesty for a dispatched worker's model pin
trigger: a worker harness is launched with a pinned model/variant
outcome: launch_state and variant_verified never overstate what was actually confirmed by the harness

statement: Every coordinator-pane path (ambient, explicit --coordinator-pane, or managed) is verified against the live tmux server confirming the pane exists, is not dead, and reports back the same pane id, refusing an absent, stale, or forged identity; the managed pane never starts a tmux server itself, and its reader displays each received line without ever executing it, so an injected notification can never become a shell command.

source.locator: README.md, "Dispatching without an interactive coordinator pane"
source.quote:
The two options cannot be combined. Every path — ambient, explicit, and managed
— goes through one verification: the live tmux server must confirm the pane
exists, is not dead, and reports back the same pane id, so an absent, stale, or
forged identity is refused rather than adopted.

`--managed-coordinator-pane` deliberately does **not** start a tmux server; a
coordinator must already be able to reach a live one, so a headless environment
fails loudly instead of acquiring a pane nobody can obser

trigger: sgt-dispatch resolves a coordinator pane by any of the three paths
outcome: only a live, server-confirmed pane is bound, and the managed pane's reader treats received content as display-only, never as commands

statement: no-mistakes is never invoked with --yes; --skip is used only for stages already proven irrelevant, and skipping a stage is never treated as a substitute for a check that was not actually performed.

source.quote: Do not use `--yes`. Use `--skip=<steps>` only for stages already proven irrelevant (e.g. `--skip=document` for changes that cannot affect docs). Skipping is not a substitute for checks that have not been performed.

trigger: no-mistakes axi run is about to be started
outcome: no run auto-approves via --yes, and any skipped stage reflects a proven-irrelevant judgment, not an unperformed check

statement: Routine dispatched workers do not invoke no-mistakes for ordinary completion, prototypes, investigations, documentation drafts, intermediate commits, or remediation loops; the coordinator starts a single run only after the implementation branch is committed and native validation is complete.

source.quote: Routine dispatched workers do not invoke no-mistakes for ordinary completion, prototypes, investigations, documentation drafts, intermediate commits, or remediation loops. The coordinator starts a single run only after the implementation branch is committed and native validation is complete.

trigger: a dispatched worker reaches any of the listed routine states
outcome: no-mistakes runs are started exclusively by the coordinator, exactly once, after native validation completes

statement: At an ask-user gate the finding is relayed to the user and the driver waits for their decision; it is never approved, fixed, or skipped autonomously.

source.quote:
- **`auto-fix`** — authorize selectively: `no-mistakes axi respond --action fix --findings <ids>`. Review the exact finding first.
- **`ask-user`** — relay to the user and wait for their decision. Never approve, fix, or skip autonomously.
- **`no-op`** — informational; approve the gate.

trigger: a gate finding is dispositioned ask-user
outcome: an ask-user gate always reaches a real human decision before proceeding

statement: While a no-mistakes run is active, the pipeline-owned worktree is not edited, the run is not aborted or rerun to escape a gate, and all pipeline-created commits are preserved; abort is used only to intentionally discard the entire run.

source.quote: While a run is active: do not edit the pipeline-owned worktree, do not abort or rerun to escape a gate, and preserve all pipeline-created commits. Abort only when intentionally discarding the entire run.

trigger: a no-mistakes run is active
outcome: the pipeline's worktree and commit history stay intact for the run's duration, and gates cannot be evaded by aborting

statement: Driving the shipping-gate run stops at checks-passed; the PR is then ready and no-mistakes continues monitoring it in the background, so the coordinator does not poll or wait for merge.

source.quote: Stop driving at `checks-passed`. The PR is ready; no-mistakes monitors it in the background. Do not poll or wait for merge.

trigger: a no-mistakes run reaches checks-passed
outcome: the coordinator disengages from active driving at checks-passed rather than polling toward merge

statement: If a no-mistakes run's outcome is failed or cancelled, branch_sync state selects the recovery action (sync, continue_active_run, or recover_custody via the matching no-mistakes axi subcommand), and a reset, stash, force-push, or branch replacement is never improvised around a blocked sync state.

source.quote:
If the outcome is `failed` or `cancelled`, inspect `branch_sync` state first:
- `sync` → run `no-mistakes axi sync`
- `continue_active_run` → keep driving the reported run
- `recover_custody` → use `no-mistakes axi sync --recover`

Never improvise a reset, stash, force-push, or branch replacement around a blocked sync state.

trigger: a no-mistakes run ends failed or cancelled
outcome: recovery follows the reported branch_sync action exactly; no ad hoc git surgery is substituted

statement: A no-mistakes run is validation-only and must not fix findings itself; actionable findings are routed into separate, deduplicated owning-repo td tasks with sgt-no-mistakes-finding.

source.quote: The run is validation-only: it must not fix findings. Route actionable findings into separate, deduplicated owning-repo td tasks with `sgt-no-mistakes-finding`.

trigger: the shipping-gate run surfaces an actionable finding
outcome: findings become td tasks in the owning repo rather than being fixed inline by the gate run

statement: Correctness, security, data-integrity, and test findings can never be deferred or ignored; cosmetic and evidence-only findings never create cards.

source.quote: Correctness, security, data-integrity, and test findings cannot be deferred or ignored. Cosmetic and evidence-only findings never create cards.

trigger: a finding of a given category is dispositioned
outcome: the highest-risk finding categories are barred from defer/ignore outcomes, while the lowest-risk categories never generate tracked work

statement: Generated worker briefs require one independent review per axis named in the shared required-axes definition (Standards, Spec, Readiness), plus a conditional Accessibility axis whenever frontend/UI/visual/interaction/accessibility/user-facing-output language appears in the mission, repo role, or repo group; that one definition drives both what the brief demands and what the findings router accepts, so the two cannot drift apart.

source.quote: Generated worker briefs require one independent review per axis named in `SGT_REVIEW_AXES_REQUIRED` in `bin/_sgt-review-axes.sh` — Standards, Spec, and Readiness. Frontend, UI, visual, interaction, accessibility, or user-facing output language in the mission, repo role, or repo group additionally requires the conditional Accessibility axis. That one definition drives both the axes the generated brief demands and the `--axis` values `sgt-review-findings` accepts, so the contract and the router ca

trigger: a worker brief is generated, or accessibility-relevant language appears in mission/role/group
outcome: the brief's required axes and the router's accepted axes are always the same set, with Accessibility added only when triggered

statement: Reviewer-supplied severity spellings are normalized to a canonical error/warning/info set: blocker, critical, and high become error (P1); major and medium become warning (P2); minor, low, and informational become info (P3); only the error family publishes a blocking gate.

source.quote: Set each finding's `severity` to a canonical `error`, `warning`, or `info`. The router also accepts and normalizes the spellings reviewers actually emit — `blocker`, `critical`, and `high` become `error` (P1); `major` and `medium` become `warning` (P2); `minor`, `low`, and `informational` become `info` (P3). Only the `error` family publishes a blocking gate, so reserve it for must-fix findings. The canonical set, the alias table, and the accepted axes are all printed by `sgt-review-findings` wit

trigger: a reviewer emits a severity value on a finding
outcome: every accepted spelling resolves to exactly one of three canonical severities, and only error blocks

statement: Each finding-card revision the router writes ends with a Revision block digest line over its own bytes; if a later route finds the stored card has been altered since the router wrote it (an edited value, an added line, a hand-written note, a changed title), it preserves the whole stored revision under a Superseded revision separator and labels the card needs-reconciliation, which only a human clears by merging the two accounts.

source.quote: Deduplication is scoped to the owning repo, axis, source, finding id, parent mission, and branch, so two sessions cannot collide on a generic finding id such as `spec-1`. An update never replaces a stored card: each revision the router writes ends with a `Revision block digest:` line over its own bytes, so a later route can tell whether the stored revision is still exactly what the router wrote. If anything has changed it — an edited value, an added line, a hand-written note, or a changed card t

trigger: the router is about to update a previously-written finding card
outcome: router-authored content is never silently overwritten when a human has touched the card; divergence is preserved and flagged for human reconciliation

statement: A retained review-findings artifact holds only post-redaction fields, never the reviewer's original output, and a retry re-validates every field and recomputes each content digest before anything reaches td; a route refuses to overwrite an artifact nobody has retried yet.

source.quote: The retained artifact holds only post-redaction fields, never the reviewer's original output, and a retry re-validates every field and recomputes each content digest before anything reaches td. A route will refuse rather than overwrite an artifact nobody has retried yet.

trigger: a findings route fails after parsing, and is later retried
outcome: retained artifacts never carry pre-redaction data, and an unretried artifact is never silently clobbered by a second failed route

statement: Drain admission locking uses an atomic hard link rather than flock, so the drain state directory must be writable by the invoking user and on a filesystem that supports hard links; when it is not, dispatch and respond fail closed rather than proceeding unlocked.

source.quote:
- no additional locking tool is required: drain admission locking uses an atomic
  hard link, so `flock` is deliberately not a prerequisite (macOS system
  installs and minimal images ship without it). The drain state directory
  (`$SERGEANT_CONFIG/drain`, default `~/.config/sergeant/drain`) must be
  writable by the invoking user and on a filesystem that supports hard links;
  otherwise dispatch and respond fail closed rather than proceeding unlocked.

trigger: a drain-gated operation (dispatch or respond) needs the admission lock
outcome: admission control never silently proceeds unlocked when hard-link support is unavailable — it fails closed instead
notes: mechanism named: atomic hard link; $SERGEANT_CONFIG/drain, default ~/.config/sergeant/drain

statement: Dispatching creates an isolated git worktree per repo, writes a mission brief into each, and spawns an agent in a local tmux window.

source.quote:
# Creates an isolated git worktree per repo, writes a mission brief into each,
# and spawns an agent in a local tmux window.

trigger: sgt-dispatch is invoked for one or more repos
outcome: each targeted repo gets its own isolated worktree, a written brief, and a spawned interactive agent window

statement: --adopt-branch resumes an existing branch that already carries commits absent from every remote, non-destructively; it is required to re-dispatch preserved work in a read-only-upstream repo.

source.quote:
#   --adopt-branch            Resume an existing branch that already carries commits
#                             absent from every remote (non-destructive; required to
#                             re-dispatch preserved work in a read-only-upstream repo)

trigger: a branch with unpushed, upstream-absent commits already exists for the intended dispatch target
outcome: the existing branch's commits are preserved and resumed rather than dispatch creating a fresh branch that could orphan them

statement: A dispatch can source its brief and context from a td task by id instead of requiring an inline brief string.

source.quote: #   --td <task-id>            Pull brief and context from a td task

trigger: --td <task-id> is passed to sgt-dispatch
outcome: the brief and context are pulled from the named td task rather than requiring an inline brief string

statement: Dispatch can enforce a dependency ordering across repos so a dependent repo's worker does not start until its dependency's worker finishes.

source.quote: #   --deps "repo1>repo2,..."  Dependency ordering: repo1 must finish before repo2 starts

trigger: --deps "repo1>repo2,..." is passed to sgt-dispatch
outcome: repo2's worker does not start until repo1's worker finishes

statement: The provider/model tuple used to launch a dispatched worker's harness is resolved by precedence: an explicit per-dispatch pin first, then an environment-level default, then the harness's own built-in default.

source.quote:
#   --model <tuple>           Pin provider/model[:variant] for the worker's harness
#                             (precedence: --model > SERGEANT_MODEL > harness default)

trigger: a dispatched worker's harness needs a provider/model tuple to launch
outcome: the resolved tuple follows --model > SERGEANT_MODEL > harness default precedence
notes: mechanism: SERGEANT_MODEL is the specific env var name; --model is the specific flag name.

statement: An explicitly-bound coordinator pane id is verified against the live tmux server before dispatch uses it.

source.quote:
#   --coordinator-pane <id>   Bind an explicit tmux pane id as the coordinator
#                             (verified against the live tmux server)

trigger: --coordinator-pane <id> is passed to sgt-dispatch
outcome: dispatch proceeds only once the given pane id is confirmed to exist on the live tmux server

statement: A fixed local callback profile and an opaque correlation id must be supplied together for a dispatch; supplying only one is rejected.

source.quote:
if [[ -n "$ORIGIN_PROFILE" || -n "$CORRELATION_ID" ]]; then
  [[ -n "$ORIGIN_PROFILE" && -n "$CORRELATION_ID" ]] || \

  # A durable handoff settles the accepted action lease: either it is finalized

  printf 'drained\n' > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
